title: SQL migrations II: reference data, tenant settings, business-assignment slots, api_credentials
objective: Convert the reference-and-configuration portion of the Liquibase changelogs to plain-SQL Supabase migrations: reference_items with guarded statuses, default_reference_items (global template), tenant_settings, business_assignments (fixed rm/underwriter slots), and api_credentials reshaped for the approved Q-19 first-party hashed-API-key scheme (M-08, P-04).
scope: reference_items: list_type discriminator covering request channels (broker flag), product lines, cover types (per product line), segments, industries, regions, party types, lead statuses, quote statuses (reporting_category, canonical_key, is_terminal guards), lost reasons, broker types; sort order; is_disabled with historical resolvability

tenant_settings: business rules — high-value threshold, SLA targets, expiry/stall/aging/duplicate-check thresholds, ref format templates, display currency, max attachment MB, pricing-approval gate toggle, lead_inactivity_expiry_days
business_assignments: two fixed slots (rm, underwriter), one role each per tenant

api_credentials: tenant- and broker-scoped rows storing salted HASHES of first-party API keys (never plaintext), status, rotation metadata, reveal-once semantics support — no Keycloak client references
Constraints/uniques/indexes for all of the above from changelogs, tenant-partitioned where the current schema partitions them
out_of_scope: Supabase Vault objects (explicitly none in MVP per Q-23)
implementation_details: Guarded statuses: reporting categories restricted to Open/Quoted/Won/Lost/Expired/Withdrawn (CHECK or lookup), canonical keys unique per tenant+list_type, terminal statuses flagged undisableable — enforce what the current schema enforces in SQL and leave service-level guards to the domain tasks.

api_credentials columns per Q-19: key_id (public prefix/lookup handle), key_hash (salted hash), salt or embedded hash format, tenant_id, broker_id nullable, name/label, status (active/disabled), created/rotated/last_used metadata. Storage format must support verify-only comparison; the pepper lives in env config, not the database.
Faithfully carry over the business_assignments shape from the 170-assignment-slots changelog (slot column constrained to rm|underwriter, one role per slot per tenant).
Migration headers: source changelog references + rollback notes (M-10).
Partitioning: follow the current schema's choices exactly (reference_items and tenant_settings are tenant-scoped; verify whether they are partitioned in the reference schema and mirror it).

integration: supabase db reset from clean applies I+II without error
CHECK/unique enforcement: invalid reporting_category rejected; duplicate canonical_key per tenant+list rejected; second role in the same assignment slot for a tenant rejected

api_credentials: plaintext key column does not exist; hash columns non-null; broker-scoped row requires valid broker FK once T-005 lands (deferred FK if brokers table arrives later — order tables so FKs resolve, or move broker FK creation to T-005 and note it)
Schema-shape comparison against the .NET reference database for this subset

history.message: Task generated by Planner from approved spec.md. Maps to M-08, P-04 data shape, Q-19 credential storage, A-12.
Delegated to Implementor. T-004 and T-009 run in parallel (supabase/migrations vs src/server/router+lib/errors+validation). Orchestrator owns harness JSON during parallel execution.

5 migrations (reference_items, default_reference_items, tenant_settings, business_assignments, api_credentials) + 2 test files (29 tests). Broker FK: reference schema deliberately has NO physical FK on api_credentials.broker_id (150 changelog states intra-tenant reference by convention, not FK); mirrored exactly and T-005 instructed in the migration header not to add it retroactively. Partitioning verified against the live legacy DB: api_credentials/business_assignments/reference_items/tenant_settings all LIST(tenant_id); default_reference_items unpartitioned (global template, no tenant_id). Catalog-driven pickup proven behaviourally: new tenant -> create_tenant_partitions -> rows land in the dedicated partition, not DEFAULT. Constraints mutation-tested: 5 schema mutations produced exactly 6 targeted failures; plaintext api_key column trips its test; every negative insert asserts a real SQLSTATE (23505/23514/23502). Positive boundary tests added so an over-broad constraint cannot pass by rejecting everything. NEEDS RATIFICATION: uq_reference_items_tenant_list_canonical_key is NOT in the .NET reference schema - added because T-004's own implementation_details and test_plan require canonical-key uniqueness per tenant+list_type, and duplicate 'won' rows would make conversion metrics undefined; conflicts with the adjacent 'enforce what the current schema enforces' clause. Documented in the migration header and parity-allow-listed as target-only; dropping that single constraint reverts to exact reference shape.

Evaluator PASS. Independently re-ran: supabase:reset x2 exit 0 (12 migrations apply from clean), normalized pg_dump --schema-only diff empty (only pg_dump 18's random \restrict session tokens differed), npm test 23 files/391 tests 0 skipped, typecheck 0, lint 0, stub script db:seed exits 1. Mutation reproduced first-hand: dropping uq_business_assignments_tenant_slot live turned 3 targeted tests red (SQLSTATE negative case + parity constraint/index diffs); restored, 29/29 green. Verified: every negative insert asserts a real SQLSTATE (23505/23514/23502), api_credentials has no plaintext/keycloak column and NOT NULL key_hash/key_salt, pepper exists only in env config (API_KEY_PEPPER; nowhere in migrations or DB), zero Vault objects (Q-23), partition routing proven behaviourally. RULING - uq_reference_items_tenant_list_canonical_key RATIFIED: the task's own implementation_details and test_plan explicitly require the uniqueness; the adjacent 'enforce what the current schema enforces' clause governs the SQL-vs-service split for the terminal-status guard, not this; duplicate canonical keys would make AC-073/074 conversion metrics undefined; the addition is documented in the migration header, parity-allow-listed as target-only with an honesty check proving it absent on the reference side, and revertible by dropping one constraint. AC-007 'parity' is satisfied: nothing from the reference schema is lost; a documented strengthening addition is the same class of deviation as the allow-listed Q-19 credential reshape.
